class_label: grey whale, gray whale, devilfish, Eschrichtius gibbosus, Eschrichtius rostus',
focus_areas: Ventral throat pleat geometry (to distinguish from other species)
Physical separation at the water-whale interface (depth/melting checks)
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Focus heavily on the texture of the skin. Real grey whales have very specific, irregular barnacle patterns. AI often generates repetitive or 'noise-like' textures for barnacles. Verify if the white patches look like distinct biological entities or just random noise. Also, check the lighting on the wet skin; it should have specular highlights consistent with a wet, oily surface. Crucially, verify that the ventral grooves (throat pleats) are anatomically correct for a Grey Whale, as the dorsal blowholes are not visible.
image_description: A vertical close-up of a large whale's head emerging from deep blue water. The view captures the ventral side (throat pleats) and the tip of the rostrum, covered in mottled grey skin with white barnacle encrustations. The dorsal side (top of the head where blowholes are located) is facing away from the camera or obscured by the angle. Water splashes around the base of the emergence.
